did_you_know.text: Did you know? Shechem was the place where all Israel gathered to make Rehoboam, Solomon’s son, king.
Did you know? Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had fled to Egypt to escape Solomon, returned from Egypt after he heard about the events at Shechem.
Did you know? The people asked Rehoboam to lighten the “yoke” and the heavy labor Solomon had placed on them, promising to serve Rehoboam if he granted their request.
Did you know? Rehoboam did not answer the people immediately; instead, he asked them to return to him in three days.
Did you know? The elders who had served Solomon advised Rehoboam to speak kindly to the people and win them over. In their view, this would keep the people loyal to him.
Did you know? Rehoboam rejected the elders’ advice and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
Did you know? The young advisers suggested that Rehoboam answer the people defiantly, using the image of his little finger being thicker than his father’s waist.

Did you know? After Rehoboam answered the people harshly, the outcome is presented as “a turn of events brought about by God,” fulfilling the word of the LORD spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.
Did you know? The Israelites rejected the rule of the house of David and declared, “What share do we have in David... Now look after your own house, David!” Then they returned to their tents.
Did you know? Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of the levy, to the people, but the Israelites stoned him to death. As a result, Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem.
